The Democratic Republic of Congo has summoned Uganda’s top diplomat in Kinshasa over controversial social media posts by Uganda’s military chief, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the son of President Yoweri Museveni. The posts, published on X, appeared to support a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo, sparking fresh diplomatic tensions between the neighbouring countries. Kainerugaba also defended Uganda’s military presence in eastern DR Congo, insisting that it was driven purely by security concerns. According to the BBC on Thursday, DR Congo’s foreign ministry described his remarks as ‘particularly serious,’ saying they had undermined diplomatic relations and created a major media controversy. The ministry said Uganda’s government was expected to clarify its official position and take measures to prevent similar incidents in the future. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Kainerugaba also accused the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda, known as the FDLR, of targeting members of the Bahima ethnic community, which has historical and cultural links with Uganda. His remarks come amid ongoing security challenges in eastern DR Congo, where several armed groups continue to operate. Walikale, in North Kivu province, is strategically important because of its mineral wealth, including significant tin deposits and gold mines. WHO chief pleads for peace in Ebola-hit DR Congo area CAF unveils 2027 AFCON logo ‘Chelle believes in NPFL stars’ Despite the diplomatic disagreement, Uganda and DR Congo maintain close military ties. Their forces have been conducting joint operations against the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces, or ADF, in eastern DR Congo since 2021. Uganda has also recently participated in mediation efforts between the Congolese government and an armed group led by former warlord Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province. This is not the first time Kainerugaba’s social media comments have caused tensions between the two countries. In February last year, he threatened to seize the eastern Congolese city of Bunia, claiming that members of the Bahima community were being attacked. In 2024, DR Congo also summoned Uganda’s diplomatic representative following his threats against foreign mercenaries operating in the country. Kainerugaba, who is widely regarded as a potential successor to his father, has repeatedly attracted regional attention through controversial statements on social media. His latest remarks have once again raised questions about the impact of his public statements on Uganda’s diplomatic relations with its neighbours. Uganda’s government has yet to issue an official response to the latest diplomatic protest.
